runner_dissent: Discomfort runs both ways. Bullish: Power is already at 21.4%, H2 exit margins are close to the 2028 target and 2026 orders are priced ~50% higher per kW (S); if the base should use H2 margins the right line is ~$937-959 and the price is already below it (and traded at $815-827 on 10-22/23). Bearish: the same quarter saw new signings fall from 20 to 11 GW, data-centre Electrification orders halve, and the CEO guide 2027 quarters to look like 3Q/4Q; float is the company's entire cash source (9M ex-float FCF -$4.2B) and it is being spent on buybacks and M&A; the unchanged >=$24B 2025-2028 cumulative FCF floor would leave only $3-4B for 2027-2028 - the shape of a float unwind; the 28x exit multiple was set at peak signings. I keep both load-bearing assumptions: margin evidence pushes EBITDA up, demand evidence pushes the multiple down, and taking both gives $859 vs $854. The conclusion is fragile only to taking one side. Next test: FY26 Q4 (late January 2027).
